<div class="band-narrow">
  <div class="section-head">About</div>

  <div class="prose">
    <p>I am a PhD candidate in Earth and Planetary Sciences at the University of
    Tennessee, Knoxville, advised by Dr. Bradley J. Thomson, defending Spring 2027.
    I work from Boulder, Colorado. I am looking for applied and research scientist
    roles in Earth observation, geospatial machine learning, and AI for science.</p>

    <p>[REPLACE after reading: this is a draft of your origin in my words; rewrite
    it in yours.] I came to machine learning from the geology side. I went to the
    NASA SMD AI/ML workshop in 2024, saw what these methods could do on problems I
    already cared about, and rebuilt my dissertation around them. Most of what I
    know about deep learning I taught myself in the two years since, working on a
    problem where the training data did not exist and had to be made.</p>

    <p>Most of what I do sits between a model and a scientific claim. I am
    comfortable at both ends, building and evaluating the pipeline and then
    defending what its output does and does not support. That work is not specific
    to my own field, and researchers outside it come to me for it: I have recently
    been helping a paleobiology group apply machine learning to their data
    [REPLACE: adjust the verb to match reality], and I work regularly with domain
    experts and collaborators outside academia who are not machine learning people.
    I am good at explaining novel technical work in approachable language, at
    framing why a problem matters to people who do not already work on it, and at
    making the case for a direction to the people who decide whether it gets
    resourced. I have also led junior contributors on technical work.</p>

    <p>When the tooling I need does not exist, I build it. Labels were the binding
    constraint on my dissertation work, so I built an annotation application to
    remove it, and I have since built a verification layer that enforces
    source-checking and evidence standards in my own AI-assisted workflow. I also
    spend real effort deciding whether a problem calls for a model at all. Some of
    my work has been establishing that a question was not answerable with the data
    available, which is a less satisfying result to report and a more useful one
    to have.</p>

    <p class="meta">U.S. citizen, eligible to obtain a security clearance.</p>
  </div>
</div>
